detail.body:
## Summary
- AITER MegaMoE no longer rejects `--enable-eplb`.
- Physical expert slots follow the DeepGEMM placement: routed experts, then redundant copies. `(n_routed + num_redundant_experts)` must divide the EP size.
- Logical top-k ids are mapped to physical ids before MegaMoEV2, and EPLB swaps the shuffled MXFP4 rows in place.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m py_compile` on the three changed files
- [ ] `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py -m cpu_test` (not run here: this machine has no vLLM test env)
- [ ] 8x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, same MegaMoE flags, A/B with EPLB off vs `--enable-eplb --eplb-config '{num_redundant_experts:32,step_interval:200,log_balancedness:true}'`. Bench 8k/1k at concurrency 512. The load log should move from about 0.71 to about 0.97 after the first rebalance. Do not compare absolute tok/s with SGLang.

The 8-GPU run is not in this PR.

+def test_redundant_expert_copies_into_local_slot(monkeypatch):
+    # EP=2, 4 logical + 2 redundant = 6 physical. Rank 1 owns physical 3,4,5
+    # which are logical 3, 0, 1.
+    experts = _make_experts(
+        monkeypatch,
+        ep_rank=1,
+        ep_size=2,
+        num_experts=6,
+        num_logical_experts=4,
+    )
+    weight = torch.full((INTER, HIDDEN // 2), 7, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    assert experts.weight_loader(
+        experts.w13_weight,
+        weight,
+        "w13_weight",
+        shard_id="w1",
+        expert_id=0,
+        return_success=True,
+    )
+    assert torch.all(experts.w13_weight[1, :INTER] == 7)
+    assert torch.all(experts.w13_weight[0, :INTER] == 0)
+    assert experts.weight_loader(
+        experts.w13_weight,
+        weight,
+        "w13_weight",
+        shard_id="w1",

+    def set_eplb_state(
+        self,

+    def get_expert_weights(self) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+        """Shuffled MXFP4 rows, one contiguous blob per local physical expert.
+
+        EPLB swaps these rows in place. The shuffle is per expert and stays
+        valid across a swap, so the rows must not be shuffled again.
+        """
+        rows = self.num_local_experts
+        blobs: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+        for name, tensor in (
+            ("w13_weight", self.w13_weight),
+            ("w13_weight_scale", self.w13_weight_scale),
+            ("w2_weight", self.w2_weight),
+            ("w2_scale", self.w2_weight_scale),

+            expert_load_view=eplb_state.expert_load_view,
+            logical_to_physical_map=eplb_state.logical_to_physical_map,
+            logical_replica_count=eplb_state.logical_replica_count,
+            record_enabled=eplb_state.should_record_tensor,
+            num_unpadded_tokens=num_unpadded,

issue_comments.body:
This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ChuanLi1101.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

8×MI355X results for this PR (`e2b95d2`), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` at `fe4df3df0` with these three files mounted. `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py`: 9 passed.

Both arms: `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 --no-enable-prefix-caching`. EPLB arm adds `--enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"num_redundant_experts":32,"step_interval":200,"log_balancedness":true}'`. Bench is random 8192 in / 1024 out, concurrency 512, 2048 prompts.

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|--:|--:|
| output tok/s | 4354 | 4256 (−2.2%) |
| median TPOT | 112.2 ms | 115.1 ms |
| median TTFT | 5120 ms | 4877 ms |

Rank balancedness (avg/max tokens across EP ranks) is about 0.55 with EPLB on and no rearrange (`step_interval` 1000000), and about 0.69 while rearranging every 200 steps. The server starts and rearrange is entered. This is not the ~0.97 reported for SGLang on an agentic trace.

GSM8K, 5-shot greedy, first 400 questions, after 1024 random requests (the rearrange arm had already rearranged 11 times):

| | acc |
|---|--:|
| EPLB off | 0.970 |
| EPLB on, no rearrange | 0.965 |
| EPLB on, 11 rearranges | 0.9475 |

Off-right / rearrange-wrong is 11 questions, the reverse is 2. The wrong answers are coherent solutions, not garbage. The no-rearrange arm on the same 1024-prompt traffic was 3891 tok/s vs 4103 with EPLB off.
